title: Clean Code
summary: Practical guidance on writing readable, maintainable code: meaningful names, small functions, clear error handling, and unit tests that keep a codebase easy to change.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
summary: Habits of effective developers, including avoiding duplication, building tracer-bullet prototypes, automating repetitive work, and taking ownership of your craft and career.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
summary: How databases, replication, partitioning, transactions, and stream processing work under the hood, and the trade-offs behind reliable, scalable data systems.

title: Effective Java
summary: Ninety focused items on writing better Java: object creation, generics, enums, lambdas and streams, concurrency, and serialization best practices.

title: Spring in Action
summary: A hands-on tour of the Spring framework and Spring Boot: dependency injection, building REST APIs, persisting data with Spring Data, securing apps, and reactive programming.

title: Terraform: Up and Running
summary: Infrastructure as code with Terraform: managing state, writing reusable modules, testing infrastructure, and deploying to AWS safely with a team.

title: The Phoenix Project
summary: A novel about an IT manager rescuing a failing project, used to teach DevOps ideas such as flow, feedback loops, limiting work in progress, and continuous improvement.

title: Site Reliability Engineering
summary: How large-scale production services are run: service level objectives, error budgets, monitoring and alerting, on-call practice, and blameless postmortems.

title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
summary: A practical introduction to machine learning in Python, from regression and decision trees to neural networks, training deep models, and deploying them.

title: AI Engineering
summary: Building applications on top of foundation models: prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, evaluating model outputs, and reducing latency and cost in production.

title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
summary: An end-to-end view of production ML: data engineering, feature design, model evaluation, deployment, monitoring for data drift, and continual learning.

title: Grokking Algorithms
summary: An illustrated, beginner-friendly guide to algorithms such as binary search, sorting, recursion, hash tables, breadth-first search, and dynamic programming.

title: Cracking the Coding Interview
summary: Preparation for software engineering interviews with 189 programming questions, data structure and algorithm walkthroughs, and advice on behavioral rounds.

title: Refactoring
summary: A catalog of techniques for improving the design of existing code in small, safe steps, backed by tests, with examples of common code smells and how to fix them.

title: Docker Deep Dive
summary: Containers explained from the ground up: images, Dockerfiles, networking, volumes, multi-container apps with Compose, and container security.

title: Kubernetes Up and Running
summary: Running containerized applications on Kubernetes: pods, deployments, services, config and secrets, scaling, and rolling out updates without downtime.

title: Fluent Python
summary: Idiomatic Python in depth: data model and special methods, sequences and dictionaries, functions as objects, type hints, iterators, generators, and asyncio.

title: Building Microservices
summary: Designing systems as independently deployable services: modeling service boundaries, communication styles, splitting a monolith, testing, and observability.
